Cinematic photorealistic photograph, vertical 9:16 portrait framing, shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, natural film-like color grade, realistic skin, fabric and grass textures, a real suburban backyard lawn at night. Any animated characters present are rendered as glossy vinyl designer toys with smooth shiny plastic shading, physically integrated into the live-action scene with matched lighting, soft reflections and true contact shadows, live-action hybrid family-film look. Focal subjects composed centrally with generous headroom above and below for the vertical frame. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks. The scene: a night lawn under a deep blue dusk sky, the party winding down. Mid-frame, STARRY — a tall golden five-pointed star character with a friendly cartoon face on the star body, large cartoon eyes with white sclera and blue irises, thin black eyebrows, a happy open smile, wearing a pink polka-dot cone party hat with a small blue flower on it, with rainbow-checkered fabric arms and legs, puffy white four-fingered cartoon gloves, and round shiny golden boots — waves goodbye with one puffy white glove raised. Beside Starry on the grass, the three CRASHERS — small toddler-sized creatures whose bodies are simple ROUND hooded onesies, soft round hooded baby-suit silhouettes, NOT shaped like bolts or diamonds or splats, the patterns only the FABRIC PRINT of each onesie: one onesie in orange fabric with a yellow zigzag print, one in blue fabric with a purple diamond print, one in green fabric with a multicolor paint-splatter print, each with a pale round face peeking out of its snug hood, big sparkly faceted-jewel eyes, a visible little buck tooth in its smile, rosy round blush cheeks, and a red-and-white striped cone party hat on top of the hood — wave with both hands, standing close together and clearly on-model, matching their canonical reference designs exactly (no plush-toy or toddler-photo drift, no round button eyes, no plain belly patch — full-body fabric print onesies with faceted jewel eyes and buck tooth). Facing the group at the edges of the frame, young adult friends in their 20s and 30s stand on the lawn waving back toward Starry and the Crashers. A golden sparkle trail rises softly into the night sky behind the group. No cloud or clubhouse is in frame anywhere.
Every human being in the scene is a young adult in their 20s or 30s — absolutely no human children, no babies, no toddlers, no minors, no middle-aged people, no elderly people, nobody with gray hair, no small human figures of any kind anywhere in frame or background; the only child-sized figures allowed are the three vinyl-toy Crasher mascots in their hooded onesies.
